items.title: ‘I want people coming back to work in the office’: B.C.’s incoming premier faces union pushback
items.summary: The battle over where B.C. government employees work is shaping up to be an early test for the province’s incoming premier, with the union representing more than 95,000 workers preparing to challenge any sweeping return-to-office order.

items.title: One person seriously hurt after crash with police cruiser, SIU invokes mandate
items.summary: A crash involving a police vehicle has shut down a road in Bradford Friday during rush hour.

items.title: Man wanted after allegedly breaking into midtown Toronto condo building’s garage
items.summary: Police are searching for a man who allegedly broke into a midtown Toronto condo building’s parking garage last month and tried to steal with several bicycles.

items.title: As Canada invests in oil and gas, environment minister boasts of 'warm welcome' at COP31
items.summary: The Liberal government's recent investments in the oil-and-gas industry have raised the hackles of climate scientists and environmental advocates. But Environment Minister Julie Dabrusin says Canada has been getting a warm reception at the COP31 United Nations climate conference in Turkey.

Ontario minister suggests purpose behind meeting with Stellantis CEO is to ‘buy some time’ amid sale of Brampton plant
items.summary: Officials in Ontario are hoping that an upcoming meeting with the CEO of Stellantis could help buy some time to explore options for keeping auto manufacturing jobs at a Brampton facility slated to be sold off.

items.title: Family, police believe missing Ontario teen is in Saskatchewan
items.summary: On Friday, Saskatchewan RCMP shared a news release on behalf of Durham Regional Police asking for the public's help finding Cairo. The 14-year-old was last seen in Courtice, about an hour outside Toronto, on Sept. 20.

items.title: Incoming Toronto city council expected to be more aligned with Olivia Chow's priorities
E-scooter rider hit by car near Moss Park
items.summary: Toronto police are investigating after a woman riding an e-scooter was hit by a car in the city’s Moss Park neighbourhood on Friday. Emergency crews were called to the area of Sherbourne and Shuter Streets at approximately 6:40 p.m. for reports of a collision.

items.title: Pax Silica means peace. In the Philippines, it’s a fight
items.summary: Outside the Grand Hyatt hotel in Manila earlier this year, five people were arrested as hundreds of activists chanting “Junk Pax Silica!” clashed with anti-riot police.

items.title: Woman arrested for allegedly making anti-transgender remarks, assaulting person walking dog
items.summary: A Toronto woman is facing charges in what Toronto police describe as a suspected “hate-motivated assault” in the city’s west end earlier this week. Detectives said a person was walking their dog on Nov. 10, when they were approached by a suspect near Lansdowne Avenue and Dupont Street.
